(PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ASHOK S. KINAGI) This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'M.V.Act, 1988" for short) by the appellant-claimant being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded vide judgment and award dated 04.02.2019, passed in MVC No.610/2018 by the learned MACT-II,
Ballari (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal' for short).
The appellant-claimant has also filed an application seeking condonation of delay of 2437 days in filing the appeal.
2. In support of the application, the appellant filed an affidavit stating that the Tribunal awarded meagre compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.

It is stated that after passing the judgment and award, his advocate informed him about the same; however, he could not contact his advocate as he was out of NC: 2026:KHC-D:3327 HC-KAR station for some time.
After a few days, he approached his advocate, who advised him to file an appeal.
It is stated that his advocate applied for a certified copy of the judgment on 10.12.2024, and the same was collected on 09.06.2025.
After collecting the certified copy, he filed the appeal before this Court.
3. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant-claimant submits that the appellant sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, and after disposal of the claim petition could not contact his advocate to file an appeal, as he was out of station for some time.
Hence, there is a delay in filing the appeal.
He therefore, prays that the delay of 2437 days in filing the appeal, be condoned.

5. Perused the records and considered the submission of the learned counsel for the appellant.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3327 HC-KAR 6.
The appellant-claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V. Act seeking a compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The Tribunal, vide judgment and award dated 04.02.2019, allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs. 4,00,450/- with interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of the petition till the entire amount is deposited, payable by respondent Nos. 1 and 2, i.e., owner and the Sri B Purushothama S/O Muniswamy vs Sri M Nagaraj Babu S/O Late Mareppa on 3 March, 2026

7. The appellant has contended that he could not contact his advocate to file an appeal as he was out of station for some time.
However, to substantiate this contention, the appellant has not produced any material to show that he was out of station.
It is further contended that he applied for a certified copy of the judgment on 10.12.2024 and collected the same on 09.06.2025.
Even in collecting the certified copy of the judgment and award, there is a delay of more than six months.
This itself goes to show that the appellant-claimant was negligent in obtaining NC: 2026:KHC-D:3327 HC-KAR the certified copy of the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
8. The Court should bear in mind while exercising jurisdiction.

It has the duty to protect the rights of the citizen, but simultaneously, it has to keep itself alive to the primary principle that when an aggrieved person without reason approaches the Court, on their leisure or pleasure, the Court be under a legal obligation to scrutinize whether the lis is at a belated stage, should be entertained or not.
It may be noted that delay comes in the way of equity.
In certain circumstances, delay and laches may not be a fatal, but in most circumstances, the inordinate delay would only invite disaster for the litigant who knocks at the door of the Court.

Delay reflects inactivity and inaction on the part of a litigant - a litigant who has forgotten the basic norms, namely, "procrastination is the greatest thief of time" and second, law does not permit one to sleep and rise like a phoenix.
The delay does bring in hazards and causes injury to the lis.

A Court is not expected to give indulgence to such NC:
2026:KHC-D:3327 HC-KAR indolent persons - who compete with 'Kumbhakarna' or, for that matter, 'Rip Van Winkle'.
Thus, there is delay in filing the appeal.
Such an inordinate delay in filing an appeal does not deserve any indulgence.
Hence, on the grounds of delay and laches, the appeal is liable to be dismissed at the very threshold.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of CHENNAI METROPOLITAN WATER SUPPLY AND SEWERAGE BOARD AND OTHERS VS. T.T.MURALI BABU reported in 2014(4) SCC 108, declined to condone the delay of four years in approaching the Court.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of MAJJI SANNEMMA @ SANYASIRAO VS. REDDY SRIDEVI & ORS., in Civil Appeal No.7696/2021 disposed of on 16.12.2021 relying on the judgment of the said Court in the case of BASAVARAJ AND ANOTHER VS. SPECIAL LAND ACQUISITION OFFICER reported in (2013)14 SCC 81 has observed as under:
"The expression "sufficient cause" cannot be liberally interpreted if negligence,
inaction or lack of bona fides is attributed to the party."

It is further observed that, NC: 2026:KHC-D:3327 HC-KAR "Even though limitation may harshly affect the rights of a party but it has to be applied with all its rigour when prescribed by statute."
It is further observed that,-
"In case a party has acted with negligence, lack of bonaf ides or there is inaction then there cannot be any justified ground for condoning the delay even by imposing conditions."

It is observed that, "Each application for condonation of delay has to be decided within the framework laid down by this Court".

It is further observed that, "If Courts start condoning delay where no sufficient cause is made out by imposing conditions then that would amount to violation of statutory principles and showing utter disregard to the legislature."
9.

Further, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Lingeswaran Etc. vs. Thirunagalingam in Special Leave to Appeal (C) Nos.2054-2055/2022 disposed of on 25.02.2022, held that when it is found that the delay is not properly explained, the application to condone the delay is required to be dismissed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court declined to condone the delay of 467 days.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3327 HC-KAR 10.
In view of the proposition laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, the appellant-claimant has not shown sufficient cause for condonation of delay of 2437 days in filing the appeal.

Accordingly,
I.A.No.1/2026 is rejected.
11. Consequently, the appeal stands dismissed.
